doc.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Touring in Japan and motherhood
summary: She tours Japan every year and says she cut back from when her son was seven to raise her children.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And you’re traveling like crazy these days, right?

Japan — I’m always in Japan. Yeah. I go there at least once a year, usually twice. Have been as many as three and four times a year. I have been in Japan and Tokyo more than I’ve been in Chicago the last five years. My daughters are now young women, they’re 19 and 20. I have a grown son. But from the time my son, who will be 33, was 7, I backed off in order to be a mother. I worked enough. But it always was in perspective. The girls are now, I’m working now for me, and I’m working to not work. And I’m going to be out here a little bit more, and have been for the last two or three years. I’m very busy these days, yeah.
